      <title>Impervious City shrug off chaos and controversy to silence Anfield | Andy Hunter</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/impervious-city-shrug-off-chaos-and-controversy-to-silence-anfield</link>
      <description><p>What had been billed as a day of reckoning for the Premier League champions turned into a Sunday afternoon stroll</p><p>Anfield welcomed Manchester City to their new reality, a sullied place where every touch is accompanied by cries of “cheat”, any favourable decision is considered proof of further conspiracy and every victory hollow. But Welcome to Hell this was not. The only body of irrefutable evidence in City’s favour <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/29/manchester-city-found-guilty-all-premier-league-charges-rule-breaches">since the guilty verdicts landed</a> is that Enzo Maresca’s league leaders appear immune to prosecution and persecution.</p><p>That may well change depending on the outcome of City’s appeal and any punishment that eventually arises, likewise the merits and value of a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/liverpool-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">commanding 3-0 win</a> on Liverpool soil. The sight of Erling Haaland savouring a statement victory in front of City’s supporters after the final whistle, while chants of “going down” echoed around the rest of the stadium, captured the schism at the heart of this Premier League season.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/impervious-city-shrug-off-chaos-and-controversy-to-silence-anfield">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘We make our own noise’: Maresca hails Manchester City after Liverpool triumph</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/enzo-maresca-manchester-city-liverpool-premier-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>‘You cannot imagine how happy I am … I’m here to win’</p></li><li><p>City win 3-0 at Anfield in first game since guilty verdict</p></li></ul><p>Enzo Maresca praised Manchester City for “making their own noise” at Liverpool as they brushed aside the controversy and threats surrounding the club with a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/liverpool-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">comprehensive 3-0 win</a> at Anfield.</p><p>City, in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/tension-banners-and-inflatable-bananas-manchester-citys-welcome-to-anfield">their first outing</a> since the club were found guilty on 114 charges relating to Premier League financial rules, maintained their 100% start to the season courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland, the excellent Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki. A sixth successive league win ensured Maresca equalled the best start to a managerial reign in Premier League history and kept City at the top of the table.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/enzo-maresca-manchester-city-liverpool-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League returns in shadow of Manchester City’s judgment day | Jonathan Wilson</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/premier-league-returns-in-shadow-of-manchester-citys-judgment-day</link>
      <description><p>Football felt secondary on the first weekend of action since club were found guilty of breaking financial rules</p><p>The Cimbri are heading menacingly south, but in Rome life goes on. The asteroid is definitely coming this way, but people go to work, eat, drink, plan as usual. The White Walkers are approaching the Wall, but the squabbles between the great houses go on. Everyone in the Premier League knows the crisis is approaching, thinks – hopes, fears? – it may be apocalyptic, but until it arrives, what can you do but carry on?</p><p>After any break, there’s always an awkward moment while everybody resets. What was the cliffhanger we left the soap opera on? What new plotline had just been seeded? This is one of the reasons international weeks are so disruptive. It’s not just that the Premier League story slows for a while, it’s that we are reminded that these entities are not eternal but alliances of convenience between paid employees who have a life outside the soap opera.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/premier-league-returns-in-shadow-of-manchester-citys-judgment-day">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Tension, ‘cheat’ banners and inflatable bananas: Manchester City’s welcome to Anfield</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/tension-banners-and-inflatable-bananas-manchester-citys-welcome-to-anfield</link>
      <description><p>A lively atmosphere greeted the former Premier League champions for their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial fair play rules</p><p>Fans lined the streets of Anfield in preparation for the arrival of the Manchester City team bus, with pyrotechnics and pure vitriol adding to the tense pre-match atmosphere. Every vantage point was taken, with spectators standing on walls to get a glimpse of the enemy, only for the coach to sneak in from the opposite side of the ground to avoid confrontation.</p><p>The subterfuge defused a volatile situation that could have turned into an incendiary one. Tensions were high on Merseyside. Since the City takeover in 2008, Liverpool have finished second to their rivals on three occasions, although only one of those falls within the parameters of the investigation into <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/29/manchester-city-found-guilty-all-premier-league-charges-rule-breaches">City’s financial breaches of Premier League rules</a>.       <title>Pino finishes off Nottingham Forest on Glasner’s unhappy Crystal Palace return</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/crystal-palace-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>It is fair to say Oliver Glasner has had more enjoyable afternoons. The Nottingham Forest head coach arrived in south London dressed like a bouncer from All Bar One in a black bomber jacket, as if he was anticipating trouble, but was instead given a rapturous reception by the home fans who used to worship him.</p><p>The generosity towards their former manager seemed to have extended to Palace’s players as Dan Ndoye was handed a goal in the third minute. Pierre Sage’s side were awful in the opening 40 minutes. Yet Forest could not find a way to beat Walter Benítez again as Liam Delap missed a golden chance to extend their lead and the Argentina goalkeeper’s heroics inspired a thrilling comeback that secured Sage’s first home victory in the Premier League since taking over from Glasner in the summer.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/11/crystal-palace-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms</p><p>Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863.
